events.title: Benedict II is consecrated pope after imperial approval
events.description: Benedict II was consecrated bishop of Rome after receiving the approval of the Byzantine emperor, as popes then required. He was the last pope to need the emperor's confirmation; his successors needed only that of the exarch of Ravenna.

events.title: Mongols crush the Seljuks of Rûm at Köse Dağ
events.description: A Mongol army under Baiju defeated Sultan Kaykhusraw II in north-eastern Anatolia. The Seljuk sultanate became a Mongol vassal and broke into the principalities from which the Ottomans emerged.

events.title: Przemysł II is crowned King of Poland at Gniezno
events.description: Przemysł II, Duke of Greater Poland, was crowned King of Poland in Gniezno Cathedral, the first royal coronation in Poland for over two centuries. He returned Poland to the rank of kingdom but was murdered at Rogoźno the following February.

events.title: The Council of Pisa elects Alexander V, a third rival pope
events.description: Having declared Gregory XII of Rome and Benedict XIII of Avignon deposed, the Council of Pisa elected Peter of Candia as Alexander V, a third claimant in the Western Schism. He died in 1410 and is now regarded as an antipope.

events.title: Warwick and the Earl of March land at Sandwich
events.description: Richard Neville, Earl of Warwick, landed at Sandwich with a rebel army and the Earls of Salisbury and March, and the three earls rode to London. Warwick and March went on to take King Henry captive at Northampton on 10 July.

events.title: George IV dies at Windsor
events.description: The former Prince Regent, known for extravagance and his patronage of architecture, died at 67. His brother William IV succeeded him, and the Great Reform Act followed in 1832.

events.title: Queen Victoria presents the first Victoria Crosses
events.description: In Hyde Park, Queen Victoria decorated 62 servicemen for valour in the Crimean War. The Victoria Cross remains Britain's highest award for gallantry.
events.html: In Hyde Park, Queen Victoria decorated 62 servicemen for valour in the Crimean War. The Victoria Cross remains Britain's highest award for gallantry.
profile: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

events.title: United Nations Charter is signed in San Francisco
events.description: Delegates of 50 nations signed the Charter creating the United Nations to maintain peace and security. It came into force in October 1945.

events.title: Kennedy tells West Berlin 'Ich bin ein Berliner'
events.description: Speaking at Rathaus Schöneberg to a crowd of about 450,000, President Kennedy declared solidarity with the people of the walled city two years after the Berlin Wall went up.
